free_text.inst.v2.D8: I read it straight through; it takes four minutes. Most of it is the sort of thing anyone would nod at - steady, self-reliant, happier leading than following. Well, yes. I have run my own companies since 1976 and I was a stockbroker before that; you do not need a chart for it. The one place it is specific it is also right, and it says so itself: marriage. I married Andy Stewart in July 1961, when I was nineteen and a sophomore at Barnard. We had Alexis in 1965. He left in 1987, the divorce was final in 1990, and I have not married since. That is the whole of it, and it was the worst thing that ever happened to me - worse than the trial. It also says time away from home is a hard place, and I spent five months at Alderson in West Virginia from October 2004, so make of that what you like. Now the wrong parts. It calls my father good fortune. My father taught me to garden, and to do a thing properly or not at all, and he was also a frustrated salesman who drank and ruled that house, and he was dead at sixty-three. That is not luck. It calls illness a difficulty. I am eighty-five this month and I have never spent a night in a hospital except to have my daughter; I do not take pills; I ride, I do yoga, I sleep four hours. It calls partnership a difficulty. Everything I built was a partnership - Time Inc., Kmart from 1987, Macy's, Sequential in 2015. Some of them ended in court, that is business. And it hedges on land and property, which is the one thing in my life that has never once disappointed me: Turkey Hill, Skylands, the farm in Bedford. Worth paying for? No. I would want my money back, and I would want the five months back.

(1) The reading calls 'luck, higher study and your father' favourable; Edward Kostyra was a domineering, drinking, frequently-out-of-work salesman who died at 63 in 1979, and the relationship is documented as conflicted by Martha herself - so A10 conflicted, A11 reversal, C9 opt2 at confidence 4, against the reading. (4) It calls home/property merely 'mixed'; property is arguably the single most successful thread of her life (Turkey Hill 1972, Skylands, Cantitoe Corners) - C4 opt2 at 5, C10 opt1 at 4.
